key_insight: APOLLAI detected stroke-related neurological deficits with higher global sensitivity than EMS personnel (78.5% vs 59.4%) and similar specificity (87.0% vs 85.9%).
clinical_relevance: This multimodal AI could support more consistent prehospital recognition of stroke-related deficits as an adjunct to EMS assessment.
method: Prospective study of video and audio recordings from 295 patients with suspected stroke at Nimes University Hospital.
Combined computer vision and audio-based deep learning with an SVM fusion classifier to assess five neurological deficits.
Compared AI and EMS assessments against consensus labels derived from seven certified stroke neurologists.
evidence_signal: Against expert consensus, APOLLAI achieved a global AUC of 0.882, with higher sensitivity than EMS across all five assessed neurological tasks.
watch_item: Hospital-recorded performance requires prospective validation under real-world EMS conditions before prehospital deployment.
paper_title: APOLLAI, a multimodal AI system, versus EMS personnel for prehospital detection of stroke-related deficits
